scope: Single frozen public passage, not full repository

claims.description: Regulations do not require periodic weighing of privately owned and operated aircraft.
claims.name: Regulations do not require periodic weighing of privately owned and operated aircraft

claims.description: Privately owned and operated aircraft are usually weighed when originally certificated or after major alterations that can affect the weight and balance.
claims.name: usually weighed when originally certificated or after major alterations that can affect the weight and balance

claims.description: The primary purpose of aircraft weight and balance control is safety.
claims.name: primary purpose is safety

claims.description: Manufacturers conduct extensive flight tests to establish loading limits for their aircraft because limit information is critical for safe flight.
claims.name: Manufacturers conduct extensive flight tests to establish loading limits for their aircraft

claims.description: A secondary purpose of aircraft weight and balance control is to aid efficiency during flight.
claims.name: secondary purpose is to aid efficiency during flight

claims.description: Overloading of the aircraft is not the only concern; the distribution of the weight is important also.
claims.name: Overloading of the aircraft is not the only concern; the distribution of the weight is important also

claims.description: Any loading that places the CG outside the established limits seriously impairs controllability of the aircraft.
claims.name: Any loading that places the CG outside the established limits seriously impairs controllability of the aircraft

claims.description: Each Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) certificated mechanic or repairman maintaining an aircraft must be fully aware of his or her responsibility to provide the pilot with current and accurate information for the actual weight of the aircraft and the location of the CG.
claims.name: each Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) certificated mechanic or repairman maintaining an aircraft must be fully aware of his or her responsibility

claims.description: Each FAA certificated mechanic or repairman maintaining an aircraft is responsible for providing the pilot with current and accurate information for the actual weight of the aircraft and the location of the CG.
claims.entity: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) certificated mechanic or repairman maintaining an aircraft
claims.name: responsibility to provide the pilot with current and accurate information

claims.description: The pilot in command (PIC) is responsible for knowing the weight of the load, CG, maximum allowable weight, and CG limits of the aircraft.
claims.name: responsible for knowing the weight of the load, CG, maximum allowable weight, and CG limits of the aircraft

claims.description: The weight and balance report must include an equipment list showing weights and moment arms of all required and optional items of equipment included in the certificate empty weight.
